comparator.academicYear: Indicative 2027–2028 prospective year programmes (concurrent cohorts), checked 2026-09-25
comparator.route: Ordinary Rechtsgeleerdheid bachelor with first-listed year-two and year-three restricted options
comparator.sourceNotes: The official current prospective 2027–28 year overviews reconcile to 60+60+60=180 EC. Year one is common to the law bachelors; year two has 55 EC compulsory public/criminal-law and professional/research courses plus one restricted 5-EC choice, instantiated as first-listed Arbeidsrecht. Year three has 47 EC compulsory private/corporate/EU law, moot-court work and a 5-EC bachelor thesis; one restricted 4-EC private-law option is Huurrecht, one restricted 4-EC integration option is AI en recht, and the first-listed 5-EC meta-legal choice is criminology 4 EC together with its matching essay 1 EC. The choices are one coherent neutral instance, not universally compulsory subjects. The year-one zero-credit Tutoraat is excluded. The programme has no ordinary reserved exchange semester. The pages are prospective and show concurrent year cohorts, not a guaranteed single-entrant schedule.

alternatives.label: Law, public institutions and society
alternatives.concept: The closest interdisciplinary UCR response studies constitutional, criminal, international, EU and private law together with public institutions, economic regulation, justice and legal argument. It cannot reproduce Radboud’s 180-EC Dutch doctrinal sequence, procedural training, moot courts or Dutch-law thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: The courses combine substantive law with politics, sociology and economic governance, so a law-and-institutions label accurately signals breadth and legal limitations.
progression: Law, Society & Justice precedes all formally dependent law courses; business and methods foundations precede their dependent advanced courses, and every term is offered.

alternatives.label: Private law, business and economic governance
alternatives.concept: This route retains the foundation in public, comparative and international law while emphasising private legal relationships, transnational business law, contracts, economic institutions, banking and commercial governance. It represents the private-law and business interests in the target but does not qualify graduates in Dutch civil procedure or professional legal practice.
alternatives.labelReason: Several private/commercial-law, business, finance and economic-policy courses shape the actual curriculum; the combined label does not imply a Dutch law qualification.
progression: The introductory law and entrepreneurship courses precede formally dependent commercial-law courses, and statistics precedes advanced economics; all planned terms are offered.
alternatives.distinctness: The route replaces comparative public institutions, conflict and social-movement courses with finance, microeconomics, econometrics and international business governance, a sustained response to private legal and commercial relationships rather than a change of label alone.

routeSelection.route: Ordinary Rechtsgeleerdheid bachelor with first-listed year-two and year-three restricted options
routeSelection.basis: The generic Dutch law bachelor has no named specialization. Its restricted options must be instantiated for one 180-EC comparator; first listed options in each choice group were selected without reference to UCR fit. Alternative valid choices remain documented and are never combined.

selection.assessment: The broad law/public institutions programme is the closest defensible interdisciplinary UCR response. Private-law and business interests support a substantially distinct second curriculum. A proposed third public-law or justice-philosophy alternative would largely rearrange the already-used seven UCR law courses with nearby politics and sociology, and the available catalogue does not support a third independently coherent Dutch-law sequence.

notes.text: UCR teaches general/comparative private, criminal, constitutional, international, EU and human-rights law alongside political, business and social study. Radboud requires a much denser Dutch public and civil-law curriculum, procedure, simulated court practice and a legal bachelor thesis. UCR study is not a Dutch Rechtsgeleerdheid law qualification and does not establish access to regulated legal professions.
